text:
Marathon Petroleum's stock fell 0.08% today and is down 10.65% over the past two weeks, tracking a sharp collapse in oil prices driven by peace hopes in the Iran conflict. Brent crude dipped below $90 per barrel on November 10th—the lowest since August—after President Trump signaled the conflict would "end fairly soon." Lower crude prices directly squeeze refiner margins, since refiners buy oil as a raw material and sell refined products like gasoline and diesel; when crude drops faster than those products do, profits narrow. The stock's two-week decline reflects this deterioration, even as U.S. refineries run at a healthy 94.5% utilization.

The backdrop adds complexity: while crude fell on conflict de-escalation hopes, State Department officials including Marco Rubio expressed skepticism about a real diplomatic breakthrough, suggesting the peace outlook remains uncertain. Additionally, last week's midterm election results included losses for Trump and the GOP, which could embolden renewable energy policies—a longer-term headwind for traditional refiners. Today's tiny move suggests the market has already priced in most of the recent crude decline and is waiting for clearer signals on whether lower oil prices stick.
